temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary has been working excessively long hours, skipping meals and sleep. He invites Gary to a weekend retreat; Gary declines, saying he appreciates the concern but cannot leave because there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Before this, Ethan sees Gary as a dedicated friend and hospital worker, without a formed belief that Gary's work habits are an urgent health concern.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Ethan forms the belief that Gary is seriously overworked and may be resistant to taking a break.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is overworking to an unhealthy degree and likely feels unable to step away from hospital duties; Ethan is concerned and wants to help.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To intervene by encouraging Gary to rest and reduce his workload; after the refusal, to keep looking for ways to support him.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes Gary's restless behavior and avoidance of discussions about work. Gary says it is complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan with his problems.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is overworked mainly because of hospital duties and is resistant to taking a break.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. He begins to suspect there is more to Gary's overworking than professional obligations, possibly personal or complicated reasons.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is carrying a deeper burden beyond ordinary hospital workload; Ethan wants to understand and help.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To confront Gary gently and encourage him to open up, offering nonjudgmental support.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and the personal challenges he is facing. Ethan learns the reasons behind Gary's overwork.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects Gary's overwork has deeper causes beyond professional obligations, but he does not yet know the specifics.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. He now understands that Gary's overwork is driven by new-department pressures plus personal challenges.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary's situation is complex but understandable; with prioritization, delegation, and support, Gary can work toward better balance.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find a better balance, starting by prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan checks in regularly and discusses Gary's progress and remaining challenges. Gary reports improvement, says he is not as overwhelmed, and had time for a movie last weekend.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has agreed to work on balance and has support, but he may be uncertain whether Gary will sustain the changes over time.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. His belief that Gary can improve is reinforced; he sees evidence that support and effort are producing progress.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is making genuine progress toward a healthier work-life balance, though he still faces challenges.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue checking in, offering support and encouragement, and being available whenever Gary needs to talk.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Ethan sees that Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and can manage on his own. Gary thanks Ethan and says he feels more in control.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is progressing but still benefits from regular support and encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. He shifts from believing Gary needs ongoing support to believing Gary is capable of managing independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary has achieved a sustainable balance and no longer needs Ethan's active intervention, though Ethan remains available if needed.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Satisfied and happy for his friend
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back and let Gary manage on his own, while letting Gary know he can still call if needed.
